title: test:changed has the same zero-selection ambiguity, flagged twice and never actioned
description:
Surfaced by TASK-192's seam audit as the one seam in its class that fell outside that ticket's file scope. This is the third time the defect class has been confirmed and the **second time this specific instance has been flagged** — it was raised in a deep-review synthesis on 2026-07-06 (recorded as R23 in `state/sessions/20260524T000000Z-65fa92c6/artifacts/deep-review-synthesis-2026-07-06.md`) and never actioned.

**The defect.** `npm run test:changed` compares against `HEAD`, so it selects only UNCOMMITTED changes — it selects zero specs once a diff is committed, and zero specs on a clean tree. A zero-selection run is visually indistinguishable from a run where everything passed. `CLAUDE.md` documents the behaviour ("it selects zero specs once the diff is committed"), but a developer running it after committing gets a green-looking result that verified nothing.

TASK-192 closed exactly this ambiguity for `test:since` by adding self-describing `TEST_SINCE_ZERO_SELECTION` markers to `scripts/test-since.mjs`, distinguishing `reason=empty-diff` from `reason=no-spec-matched` without changing the exit code. `test:changed` has no wrapper at all — it is a bare `vitest --changed` invocation in `package.json`, so there is nowhere for a marker to live today.

**Why it matters more than it looks.** `test:changed` is the FIRST command in the per-ticket hand-off gate. A developer who commits and then runs it as a final check gets a confident green from a run that selected nothing. That is the precise sequence a careful developer would follow.

**Follow the precedent, and follow the amendment that shaped it.** TASK-192's implementer first built a hard-fail version and had to revert it: a docs-only diff legitimately selects zero specs, so a blanket non-zero exit would red-gate every docs ticket. **Do not repeat that mistake here.** The goal is a self-describing empty, not a fatal one. Read `scripts/test-since.mjs`'s header comment and the "Empty-result contract" section of `CLAUDE.md` before designing anything — both were written specifically to record that reasoning.

Note the difference from `test:since`: for `test:changed`, the "clean tree / already committed" case is the COMMON one and is entirely legitimate, so the marker matters more than any failure ever could.
acceptance_criteria: A failing spec first demonstrates the ambiguity: `npm run test:changed` on a clean tree (or immediately after committing a diff) currently produces output indistinguishable from a successful verification run. Capture the red-run output verbatim.

The seam is made self-describing following the TASK-192 precedent: a caller can tell 'zero because nothing is uncommitted' from 'zero because the selection failed' without inferring it. Reuse the marker shape and reasoning already established in scripts/test-since.mjs rather than inventing a second convention.

The change MUST NOT make a zero selection fatal. A clean tree is the common and legitimate case for this command, and a hard failure would red-gate ordinary use — the same over-application TASK-192 built and had to revert. State explicitly in the closing comment that this was considered and rejected.

The real vitest exit code is passed through unchanged — verify that a genuine test FAILURE still exits non-zero after the change. A wrapper that swallows failures would be far worse than the ambiguity it fixes.

Any added pre-check does not meaningfully slow the inner development loop. test:changed is the fast iteration command; measure the added latency and record it. If the cost is material, prefer a cheaper signal over a thorough one.
Regression locks cover both branches (zero-selection marker present; normal selection produces no marker), red-green planted.
npm run test:all is green; no existing spec regresses; CLAUDE.md's Empty-result contract section is extended to record this instance alongside the three already listed.
